summary: Measured on current-account pack pages against 14 Belgian banks, ING sits clearly with the traditional banks on the combined position score (0.211). Its sharpest over-index is on figures and percentages quoted (25.5 against a peer mean of 12.15, its largest gap at 1.62 standard deviations), while its clearest under-index is on calls to action (2.0 against a peer mean of 13.38) and it shows no comparison table where the peer mean is 0.38. Treat all of this as design observation only: the dataset mixes seven product families and two languages, and no performance data links any of these features to a click or a conversion.

recommendations.title: Add repeated, labelled calls to action down the page
recommendations.finding: Calls to action is one of only two features where ING sits below the field: 2.0 on average against a peer mean of 13.38, a gap of about one standard deviation below the market. The page also opens strongly (it scores 0.5 on opening something that stops the reader against a peer mean of 0.17), so the incoming attention is not converted into an obvious next step.
recommendations.recommendation: Place a clearly labelled open-account or apply call to action at the end of every value block, not only once on the page: one directly under the opening block, one after the fee and condition section, and one at the foot. Keep the wording of the action identical across all placements.

recommendations.title: Add an at-a-glance comparison table
recommendations.finding: ING shows no comparison table at all (0.0) while the peer mean is 0.38, one of the ten clearest gaps in the dataset. ING's offer clarity already scores above the field (4.0 against 3.5), so the missing element is the side-by-side view rather than the explanation.
recommendations.recommendation: Add a compact comparison table to the current-account page that lays out the ING pack options side by side with the monthly fee, the card, and the conditions in the table cells themselves, so the reader does not have to move between sections to compare.

recommendations.title: Cut the vertical sprawl and fold detail into expandable blocks
recommendations.finding: ING's pages run long: 9465 pixels against a peer mean of 6414.12, about 0.91 standard deviations above the field. Length here is measured as page geometry, not as word count, so a large part of it is repeated blocks and spacing rather than argument.
recommendations.recommendation: Remove or merge the lowest-value sections between the opening block and the fee section, and move long condition text into collapsed expandable blocks that stay on the page but no longer occupy the main scroll. Re-measure the page height afterwards to confirm the reduction.

recommendations.title: Keep the numbers, but pair each one with plain language
recommendations.finding: Figures and percentages quoted is ING's largest deviation from peers: 25.5 against a peer mean of 12.15, 1.62 standard deviations above the market. This is an automatic count, so it measures density of numeric claims, not whether readers understand them; the same dataset shows challenger pages scoring higher on clarity (4.67 against 3.8 for traditional banks).
recommendations.recommendation: Keep the numbers but rewrite each figure block as a pair: the figure, followed by one short sentence in plain language saying what it means for the reader's monthly cost. Cap the number of figures above the fold so the opening block stays readable.

recommendations.title: Extend the youth and student framing onto its own page
recommendations.finding: Targets students or young people scores 1.0 for ING against a peer mean of 0.38, 1.26 standard deviations above the field. This feature is model-assisted and was scored on the captured pages only, so it tells us the framing is present, not how well it lands.
recommendations.recommendation: Give the youth framing its own destination: state the age or student eligibility, the card and the fee in the first screen of the jeunes page, and use one call to action written for that audience rather than reusing the standard open-account label.

recommendations.title: Make the fast digital sign-up promise concrete on the opening-account page
recommendations.finding: ING leads the field on two related signals: promises fast digital sign-up at 0.5 against a peer mean of 0.15, and designed mobile-first at 1.0 against a peer mean of 0.5. The sign-up claim is model-assisted, so it records that the claim is made, not that it is demonstrated.
recommendations.recommendation: On the opening-account page, turn the speed claim into a short numbered sequence (what the reader needs, how many steps, what happens next), and keep that sequence in the same order on mobile and desktop layouts.

recommendations.title: Close the campaign structure with an action, not a summary
recommendations.finding: ING's campaign structure is above the field on structure completeness (3.5 against a peer mean of 3.0) and on offer clarity (4.0 against 3.5), and above average on opening attention (0.5 against 0.17). These are rubric scores carrying the judgement of the people who scored them, and inter-rater agreement is reported separately.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep the strong opening, but review the final section of each campaign page and replace any closing summary with the same call to action used in the opening block, so the page ends on an action rather than a recap.

recommendations.title: Have the current-account page finalised for the early-September window
recommendations.finding: ING's current-account terms show a cluster of search anomalies inside the available window: a sustained trend for 'compte à vue ING' on 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-06 and an isolated spike for 'ING zichtrekening' on 2026-09-06. Search interest is context, not evidence that any page or campaign worked, and the pages captured for this analysis are today's pages, not the pages live during any earlier spike. The link between this window and ING's page performance is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: Treat the early-September period as a fixed deadline: finish the current-account page copy, the comparison view and its call to action in both language versions before that window opens, rather than changing the page during it.
recommendations.market_context: Attention clustered on ING's current-account terms in the week of 2026-09-06, with a sustained trend for 'compte à vue ING' on 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-06 and an isolated spike for 'ING zichtrekening' on 2026-09-06, inside the 2021-09-12 to 2026-09-13 window.

recommendations.title: Prepare the savings pages for the same window
recommendations.finding: The term 'compte épargne ING' shows a sustained trend on 2026-09-06 and again on 2026-09-13, and the repositioning campaign rows matched to that period carry the savings product alongside the current-account product. Search interest is context only: it says people were searching, never that a page or a campaign caused anything, and the campaign matches on 2026-09-06 carry a seasonal confound. The link to page performance is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: Sequence the savings work behind the current-account page but inside the same window: check that the savings and term-account pages carry current conditions and an explicit call to action, and hold any large layout change to these pages until after the window closes.
recommendations.market_context: A sustained trend on 'compte épargne ING' appears on 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-13, the same two weeks in which ING's current-account terms moved, within the 2021-09-12 to 2026-09-13 window.

recommendations.title: Schedule current-account pushes away from the competitor's spike weeks
recommendations.finding: KBC shows nine recent anomalies on the same current-account product, as isolated spikes on 'KBC zichtrekening' in the weeks of 2026-03-22, 2026-05-17 and 2026-07-26, plus a spike on 'Compte Plus KBC' on 2025-08-10. This is context about when attention moves, not evidence that any page or campaign performed, and it is a hypothesis to verify before planning against it.
recommendations.recommendation: When choosing the weeks to push ING's current-account page and its paid support, pick weeks outside that cluster so ING's message is not competing for the same search attention, and keep the page itself unchanged during those weeks.
recommendations.market_context: Competitor attention on the same product family peaks in identifiable weeks (2026-03-22, 2026-05-17, 2026-07-26, 2025-08-31, 2025-03-16 and 2025-08-10), while ING's own current-account terms cluster in early September 2026.

recommendations.title: Audit sustainability wording on the product pages
recommendations.finding: Sustainability and climate is the largest theme in ING's 24 headlines over the last 90 days (5 headlines), including a court ruling allowing a climate case against ING to proceed and coverage of ING financing oil companies despite a climate pledge. Themes are topics, not sentiment. Whether ING's own pages currently make environmental or green claims, and how those claims read next to this coverage, is a hypothesis to verify rather than something this analysis measured.
recommendations.recommendation: Review any environmental or sustainability wording on the campaign pages and keep it to specific, verifiable statements with a source; on product-offer pages for current accounts and savings, keep the framing on fees, access and conditions instead of climate or green framing.
recommendations.reputation_context: Sustainability and climate is the largest theme in ING's 24 headlines over the last 90 days (5 of 24), with notable headlines on a climate case against ING and on ING financing oil companies despite a climate pledge.

recommendations.title: Put fees and conditions next to the action, without pressure framing
recommendations.finding: Regulatory topics account for 4 of ING's 24 headlines in the last 90 days, alongside 2 financial-results and 2 product-launch headlines. Themes record what the press is writing about, not whether anything worked, and ING's own headline set includes one crisis-or-scandal item. The connection between this coverage and how readers respond to ING's fee and condition wording is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: On the savings and term-account pages, place the fee, rate and condition wording directly beside the call to action rather than at the foot of the page, and avoid countdown or scarcity devices in that block so the offer reads as a plain statement of terms.
recommendations.reputation_context: Regulatory topics make up 4 of ING's 24 headlines in the last 90 days, with a further 2 financial-results headlines and 1 crisis-or-scandal headline in the same set.
